newsitem.title: USA: North Korea links food aid to talks, official says.
newsitem.headline: North Korea links food aid to talks, official says.

text.p: Famine-threatened North Korea, in a new round of talks on Monday with the United States and South Korea, wanted commitments for food aid before it could agree to attend negotiations on a peace treaty to end the 1950-53 Korean War, a South Korean official said.

The official said he expected the issue to be resolved by the three nations at Monday's one-day meeting in New York, the third in a series to prepare the way for four-nation negotiations which would eventually also involve China.

"Basically North Korea is taking the same position as they took in the April meeting, but we are trying to make them come around to our position," delegate Yu Myung Hwan of the South Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs told reporters.

"North Korea wanted us to commit a specific amount of food aid before they would come to the preparatory talks ... and we are trying to delink the food and the four-party talks," he said during a lunch break.
Officials from North Korea and the United States were not available for comment.
Earlier a U.S. State Department official said senior envoys from the three countries appeared relaxed, shaking hands and exchanging pleasantries before the meeting began in a New York hotel.

North Korean and South Korean delegation leaders told each other they hoped for good results from the meeting, a follow-up to earlier talks in March and April to discuss a proposal by Washington and Seoul for four-nation peace talks.

The proposed four-party negotiations would aim to replace the armistice with a formal peace treaty. The armistice ended the fighting in the 1950-53 Korean War, but technically not the war on the Korean peninsula.

According to the U.S. official, North Korean delegation leader Vice Foreign Minister Kim Gye Gwan said: "Last time we were concerned that there might be a premature baby, but this time we're not concerned about a premature baby."
The South Korean delegation is led by Deputy Foreign Minister Song Yong Shik.
Communist North Korea, threatened by famine, agreed in principle in April to join the peace talks but linked its participation to food aid and an end to U.S. trade sanctions.
Political analysts say Pyongyang has agreed to join the four-way talks in a policy shift designed to hold the reclusive state together.
They say that with famine and a ruined economy, the Stalinist government needs to repair its relationship with Western countries who could provide much-needed assistance.
In the relaxed exchanges before Monday's meeting began, U.S. delegation leader Charles Kartman joked with his counterparts, the U.S. official said.

He quoted Kartman as saying, "let me tell you about American boxing ...", a reference to Saturday's World Boxing Association heavyweight title fight in which challenger Mike Tyson was disqualified for biting both ears of champion Evander Holyfield.
